clue.text: Introduction to Homer, or superb Roman poet

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: the opening letter of the Greek poet's name
taken as written
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A comparison of the Greek epic poet with a brilliant Latin one, as in a classics lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace (Quintus Horatius Flaccus) was a celebrated lyric poet of Augustus's Rome, author of the Odes.

clue.text: Relative in his flares, bullied around start of term

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is taken
being bullied means being pushed about, so these letters are knocked out of order
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go on either side of the single letter

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A schoolchild teased about his flared trousers when the new school term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters wrap around the T, which sits between the second S and the final ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-sister shares one parent with you, so she is a family member.

clue.text: Right above pirate ship

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
over means above

explanation.surface: A buccaneer vessel positioned directly overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the R sits above the rest, which the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Rover is an old word for a sea robber, and by extension for a pirate vessel.

clue.text: Company car is damaged making for a Mediterranean island

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so these letters are bent into another order

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A firm's vehicle gets dented while heading for a holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a large French island in the Mediterranean Sea, birthplace of Napoleon.

clue.text: A crooner, fellow from an Oxfordshire town

blocks.note: taken as written
Bing Crosby, the famous American crooner
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A singer and an academic who both hail from the same English market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Abingdon is a market town near Oxford, which suits the college don in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Abingdon-on-Thames is a historic market town lying just south of Oxford, in the county of Oxfordshire.

clue.text: OU sportsman keeping a woman of intelligence

blocks.note: a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford University (OU) at a sport
stocking goods means keeping them on hand

explanation.surface: An Oxford athlete who holds on to a clever woman.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a Blue is awarded for competing for the university against the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluestocking is a dated, often mocking term for an educated, intellectual woman.

clue.text: Beat writer, at first, with a club

indicators.note: at first says the writing piece goes in front, ahead of the word for beat

blocks.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
to lick an opponent is to beat them

explanation.surface: An author being assaulted with a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old Scottish golf club with a lofted iron head, equivalent to a modern nine iron.

clue.text: During an illness, almost over, trouble a spiritual leader

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the ailment is dropped
turned over, the shortened phrase is read the other way round
during means within the span of, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a malady is an illness
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A sickness nearly behind someone, then a fresh worry for a religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: AMALADY loses its Y, is turned round, then AIL goes in after the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the chief spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Pond creature young toad initially turns into

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: new means young, recent
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A bit of fanciful natural history in which a baby toad grows into a different amphibian.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invents a metamorphosis; 'turns into' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian, a salamander that breeds in ponds.

clue.text: Irritable old servants

blocks.note: first meaning: liverish, bad-tempered, as if from a disordered liver
second meaning: in older usage, a household's uniformed retainers taken collectively

explanation.surface: A grumpy description of elderly household staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the two as adjective and noun, but they are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is an informal adjective for peevish, and archaically a collective noun for liveried retainers in a great house.

clue.text: Awfully foul brew could make one flounce

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so these letters come out in a botched order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A disgusting drink that would make anyone storm out in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounce' looks like a verb, storming off, but here it is the noun for a frill on a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a pleated ruffle or flounce sewn onto a skirt or petticoat.

clue.text: Class points out what a theatre may put on

definitions.text: what a theatre may put on

blocks.note: a variety is a class or kind
to show is to point out

explanation.surface: A teacher identifying the programme a theatre might stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety shows are stage entertainments of mixed acts such as comedy, song and juggling, staged in theatres.

clue.text: Precise, short theatre cleaner

blocks.note: as in a surgical strike: done with great precision
a short is a small measure of strong drink

explanation.surface: Praise for a neat, brief play reviewed as a clean piece of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'short' is a measure of spirits such as whisky, as opposed to a long drink. The theatre here is an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical spirit is methylated alcohol used to sterilise skin and instruments, so it cleans things in the operating room.

clue.text: Running on tenth lap in old Olympic event

indicators.note: running means in motion, so these letters move around into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An athlete still running on the tenth circuit at the ancient Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The pentathlon, five events in one contest, was part of the ancient Greek Olympic Games.

clue.text: Itinerant Romanians in an Italian-speaking country

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering about, so these letters roam into a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Travelling Romanians turning up in a small Italian-speaking state.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy, where Italian is the official language.

clue.text: Hitchcock film noir - too darned American

indicators.note: darned means mended with stitching, so these letters are worked back together differently

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A grumble that a Hitchcock thriller is far too dark and much too American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darned' reads as a mild curse but is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious is the 1946 spy thriller directed by Alfred Hitchcock, starring Cary Grant and Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Card (king) Welshman rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the name is read the other way round

blocks.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
Evan is a typically Welsh first name

explanation.surface: A cheeky Welshman spurned by a king, the bracketed word passing as a royal aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords use a common Welsh name to stand for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the jack, the court card ranking below the queen in a standard pack.

clue.text: A bye, perhaps, in over

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye, is credited to the batting side
second meaning: surplus, more than needed

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer noting a bye conceded during an over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled from one end, so the surface stays at the crease; here 'over' means surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes, leg-byes, wides and no-balls are collectively called extras in cricket; extra also means additional or left over.

clue.text: A grant secured by the sportsman?

indicators.note: held fast by something means enclosed within it, so one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to let is to grant or allow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A funding award won by a sports competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies letters that wrap around the grant.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sport, especially track and field events.

clue.text: Accept compassion is to be encouraged

blocks.note: to take something is to accept it
having heart means having compassion

explanation.surface: Advice that letting others show you kindness should lift your spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heart is an idiom meaning to gain courage or confidence, to feel encouraged.

clue.text: Rope with which Henry gets cart hauled up

indicators.note: in a down entry, hauled up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a dray is a heavy cart

explanation.surface: A man hoisting a cart using a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hauled up' suits ropes in the surface but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A halyard is a rope used on a ship for raising or lowering a sail, flag or yard.

clue.text: Two pianists, drunk

blocks.note: first meaning: two nineteenth-century composers who were also virtuoso pianists
second meaning: Cockney rhyming slang, rhyming with a vulgar word for intoxicated

explanation.surface: A pair of piano players who have had a few too many.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it; this pair of composers rhymes with 'pissed', British slang for intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms and Franz Liszt were both concert pianists, and the pairing is rhyming slang for being inebriated.

clue.text: Problems housing 50 in wretched dwellings

indicators.note: housing something means giving it a home inside, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: sums are arithmetic problems
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty families with troubles living in squalid homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' fits the surface about homes but signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Slums are overcrowded, squalid urban areas of poor housing.

clue.text: Additional matter written about learner driver

indicators.note: written about means set down around something, so one part surrounds the other

blocks.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: Extra material composed about someone taking driving lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L plate, so L stands for learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus as an adjective means extra or added, as in a plus factor.

clue.text: Free wood used to make a stall

blocks.note: loose means set free, unrestrained
box is a hard wood from the box tree

explanation.surface: Timber going cheaply to build a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a market stall; the answer is a stall for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose box is an enclosed stable compartment in which a horse can move about untethered.

clue.text: Guide by hand

blocks.note: first meaning: a handbook of instructions
second meaning: operated or done with the hands rather than automatically

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts read as one instruction, steering something by hand, but they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual is an instruction book, and manual as an adjective describes work done with the hands.

clue.text: Anxiety shown by South American writers at closing of bookstore

indicators.note: the closing of a word is its very end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation
US, the United States
pens are writing instruments
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Nervous Latin American authors waiting while their local bookshop shuts down.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tense uncertainty felt while waiting to learn an outcome.

clue.text: Small number on team backing inventor

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the combined letters are read from the end

blocks.note: No. is the short form of number
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A handful of people on a team supporting a creative genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small number' reads as a few people, but it signals the shortened form of number.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb.
